text:
Nadia: noticing a recurring correctness gap when doing soft-share handoffs + async replication. repro below.
Omar: short summary?
Nadia: tenant X holds prefix p, does local write W, acks quickly, replication to new owner Y lags. takeover begins, Y becomes authoritative for new writes, but A still serves stale slab entries for some reads.
Felix: sounds like two races: local demote TOCTOU and cross-node replication visibility.
Yuki: can you paste the minimal bad window?
Nadia: sure:
```
// read path (simplified)
if (is_resident(prefix)) {
  return slab.read(key) // assumes slab reflects authoritative state
}
// demote path
clear_residency(prefix)
enqueue_handoff(prefix)
```
Readers snapshot residency then read slab; demote clears residency but doesn't fence inflight readers. On top of that, takeover can flip authoritative owner before replication arrives.
Felix: we've talked about generation counters for the first TOCTOU. For cross-node, we discussed takeover-token with min_lsn. Both seem necessary.
Omar: agreed. combine both: prefix.gen protects local reader races, takeover token protects cross-node stale-serving.
Yuki: rough protocol sketch:
1) new_owner -> current_owner: TAKEOVER_REQUEST
2) current_owner -> new_owner: TAKEOVER_TOKEN {epoch, min_lsn}
3) current_owner sets prefix.handoff_in_progress and bump prefix.gen++
4) new_owner waits until applied_lsn >= min_lsn or timeout, then sets authoritative=true and broadcasts epoch
Readers always do: gen0 = prefix.gen; v = slab.read_if_resident(key); gen1 = prefix.gen; if (gen0 != gen1 || slab.lsn(key) < prefix.takeover_min_lsn) fallback_read()
```
Nadia: fallback_read() -> route to authoritative node or read-through backing store. cheap extra hop but preserves correctness.
Felix: what about long-lived cursor pins that prevent slab cleanup and keep stale values alive across handoffs?
Omar: treat cursor pins as pinned_at_gen. on demote bump prefix.gen so pinned items become invalid if pinned_at_gen != prefix.gen. then cursor sees CURSOR_INVALIDATED and client can retry. optionally implement transferable pins in a canary.
Yuki: perf concerns: per-read checks add two compares (gen and lsn). slab already stores a compact lsn tag per entry for GC; gen is per-prefix. overhead minimal.
Nadia: metrics/flags we should add: runtime.flags.prefix_gen_check, runtime.flags.takeover_token, runtime.flags.cursor_pin_transfer_canary. metrics: prefix.gen_mismatch_count, handoff.token_wait_ms, handoff.forced_takeovers, prefix.cursor_invalidations.
Felix: testing plan: microbench with asymmetric replication delays, long-cursor fuzz, and rapid rebalances. measure fallback read rate and extra latency.
Omar: defaults: timeout 200ms for token wait; fast-path if new_owner.applied_lsn >= min_lsn (most steady-state cases). forced takeover recorded as event.
Yuki: ops-bot create canary ticket and add playbook note please.
ops-bot: created #CANARY-945: "prefix-gen + takeover-token canary" assigned to @nadia, due 2026-04-14 :white_check_mark:
Nadia: I'll spike this week and post perf numbers. If fallback_read rate > 1% we revisit: maybe tighten replication path or make takeover wait longer for hot prefixes.
Felix: consider adaptive hysteresis for eviction to reduce churn during canary if we see noisy tenants impacting fallback rates.
Nadia: noted. will include hysteresis telemetry.
Omar: TL;DR: implement gen bump on demote + takeover-token handshake that carries min_lsn, reader-side cheap checks, and cursor invalidation semantics by default. Transferable pins optional canary.
Yuki: thanks — this reads like a good, incremental safety net. put a short RFC blurb once you have numbers and we'll review on eng-runtime sync.
Nadia: will do. ETA EOD Fri with initial numbers.
